So I like the idea. It's really dark, and disturbing, and stressful, very interesting idea. That being said, I do have issues.
The UI and physical mechanics feel real wacky, and not in the fun quirky way. Managing inventory is really frustrating and confusing at times. making inventory and control scheme related fixes to make it a bit more intuitive would be a big game changer for the better.
The second is the visual and audio effects. I'm not even epileptic and I had to stop playing because I thought I was going to have a seizure. I like how much it ramps up the stress when you're in deaths door after a long fall and cracking your head open and struggling to find some way to make it through, but good lord they need to be toned down a bit. Even outside of the physical comfort aspect, there's a certain point where they don't feel interesting and challenging, but just tedious and frustrating. I ended up developing severe brain damage and it kept causing my screen to mirror and having me run the opposide way or swing in the wrong direction. That's fine. I like that idea overall. It's just that it gets to this point of constant nonstop flicking back and forth where it almost becomes a rhythm game to move in one direction. I think all the effects and visuals and audio are awesome, they just need to be toned down a little bit. 

I'm still going to give it a recommendation under the assumption that those two things could be changed. That being said, if the UI and inventory aren't cleaned up, and the intensity of the visuals aren't toned down just a bit, then I would not be able to recommend it.

I will buy this game on a sale (as I do all games) after it releases EVEN if I NEVER intend to play it again. The demo was so amazingly effective at eliciting an emotional response for my 'character' if it can even be called that. You are the guy telling it what to do, that is your job. Living through hell is it's purpose. This hits on so many layers of what I love it is incredible. Ruthless exploitation, human cruelty, science without ethics, created life deprived of rights and treated as products... I'm not saying it is beautiful, it is cold, like being the eye of a robotic auto-surgeon in an after battle medical camp. Be cold... Be unfeeling... Bear witness to your failures. 

My first was doomed, this I knew. And within 10 minutes fate came to be. The next 2 went quickly as well. I named them all, in my head, to heighten my situational response, the names I chose I will not share, they are irrelevant. #4 went in with a more seasoned operator, and was more successful. His agonizingly painful and lengthy death made all the more disappointing. His freefall to impact, terminal struggle, and cries of agony and begging for help that could never come moved me. I tried to force him to use what was available to save his life, but he had so little and was too scared to obey... His death was far from quick. 

#5 made it to the bottom of sector 1, in terrible condition, unlocking a new layer of tutorial (Unironically brilliant decision, didn't give me the info I needed knowing most would not use it, and be disinterested.) His death was glorious. He knew he was screwed, disobeyed constantly, tore his wrists open to use the adrenaline to push on and fight the spider like creatures blocking his path and succumbed to his blood loss. He impressed me. 

From then on others took his place, learning new skills to extend survival, or utilize the environment. Some died in agony, others thankfully instantly terminal. It was in this period I found an efficient mercy killing option for when there was no hope. But I always try. I want them to succeed. The Devs added a custom difficulty option. And I finally used it. No region timers, bags last 2x as long, water does not move you. Timers when I'm this bad do not help, I barely make it now. Bags are stupidly low, but with this you replace them 'less often' but still enough to care about repairs and backups. And water interaction is VERY poorly implemented, a single 'blob' of water will move at random and force you prone and off an edge. But am I complaining? NO. Because it let me turn off what I felt was broken without reducing the actual difficulty of the game. 

I spent nearly 40 hours throwing glowing fruit down bottomless holes, trying to dig to water near death, slithering through holes and learning to avoid broken glass, bear traps, bounce plates, Impaler traps and F***ING landmines that I know the game did not get easier. My best work was saving a life twice that in the end still perished under my command. As an actual sociopath and borderline psychopath I felt a real connection to this game. Every failure has impact, every mistake was punishing, and "I'll just respawn" was never the reaction. 

There is a 'creature does not make pained noises option' I would never use. There are many options to soften the game. You can tailor this experience to suit your needs. But for those that want some taste of the black horror that the video promised, that is here in abundance. I actually am apprehensive to turn the game back on. I fear my impending failure. I fear my hopelessness. I fear my mistakes. And I only hope that the Devs NEVER backpedal from what they created. This is not meant to be hopeful, or kind, but you can find both with skill. For everything else, there's sweet oblivion. Death's merciful embrace.

[h2]Суть игры:[/h2]
Главным героем этой игры является Подопытный (в сообществе игры также известный как Эксперимент, или Экспи), которого по сюжету послали в глубину другой планеты, использовавшейся людьми как свалка, чтобы достать оттуда ненарочно отправленную туда технологию (мы даже на текущий момент толком не знаем, что это за технология вообще) и он обречён на смерть в этих опасных глубинах. Сюжет звучит достаточно интригующе и заманчиво, что делает игру чуточку интереснее.
[h2]Крафт:[/h2]
Игра выделяется среди других несколькими своими особенными фишками. Одна из них заключается в сложной системе крафта и лечении себя. Эту игру крайне трудно понять без вики или руководств с YouTube и даже я сам, когда посмотрел на рецепт бинта, и увидел, что он крафтится из двух рваных повязок, которые создаются из предмета с качеством "Рвущееся", я долго потом думал "Что же это такое, "Рвущееся"?", пока не загуглил это. Оказалось, можно было скрафтить элементарный холст из листвы и порвать его на рваную повязку.
Часть вашего выживания тут зависит от того, как быстро вы принимаете решение, что надо крафтить, что именно надо скрафтить, что вы будете крафтить потом и как быстро ваш Подопытный набирает очки интеллекта. Система крафта тут [u]примерно[/u] такая же сложная как в Terraria, но со временем все рецепты можно примерно выучить и уже так сложно не будет.
Если вы попробуете обойтись в этой игре без крафта, вам будет крайне сложно выжить здесь в дальнейшем, так как у вас банально не будет при себе необходимых инструментов, чтобы помочь себе (или товарищу, если вы играете в многопользовательском режиме (про этот опыт позже)) в экстренной ситуации.
[h2]Здоровье Подопытного и его поддержка:[/h2]
Чтобы уметь поддерживать его жизнь после несчастных случаев, желательно иметь медицинское образование, ведь система ранений и их лечений проработана до невероятности реалистично — для лечения каждого ранения и недуга необходимо своё лекарство, здесь вам предстоит узреть и побороть от банальных кровотечений до [u][b]борьбы с депрессией своими силами[/b][/u] и если вы здесь как-то неудачно упадёте, да так, что у тебя появится внутреннее кровотечение, недостаточно просто использовать бинты. Поэтому с нуля в этой игре, повторюсь, будет разобраться крайне трудно и в "Casualties: Unknown" из "Casual" вы вряд ли здесь что-то найдёте. xd
[h2]Саундтрек:[/h2]
Саундтрек к этой игре — моё почтение! Особенно "дроны" к каждой внештатной ситуации в игре, будь то когда Подопытный при смерти ("Is this the end..?"), состояние агонии ("Agony") или клиническая смерть ("[b]..![/b]")(мне особенно нравится в этом эмбиенте, как нарастает тон мелодии и увеличивается ощущение "давления", что подчёркивает ощущение, что смерть уже здесь и конец игры будет буквально через несколько секунд, если ты не играешь в многопользовательском режиме), они отлично передают состояние нависшего рока над главным героем и весь ужас ситуации, который происходит на текущий момент, что заставляет больше переживать за главного героя и лучше обдумывать свои действия, дабы не причинять ему боль лишний раз. [spoiler]признаться честно, когда я только начинал играть в эту игру и мне удавалось услышать 15-ю секунду композиции "Droning Grays" во время игры, я срался каждый раз, думая, что на меня сейчас какая-то тварь из тёмного места нападёт.[/spoiler]
[h2]Мультиплеер:[/h2]
И наконец, чего не хватает игрокам в сей игре — это [b]официальная возможность многопользовательского прохождения[/b]. Хоть остальные игроки и жалуются что его весьма не хватает игре и с ним "Casualties: Unknown" гораздо веселее, но я считаю, что в какой-то мере мультиплеер для этой игры будет лишним, т. к. он будет рушить атмосферу игры (одиночество, безнадёжность, "тебе никто не сможет помочь кроме тебя самого") и, отчасти, её изначальную задумку, но я решил попробовать этот экспириенс с фанатским модом (кому надо, ссылка на него — https://github.com/creaturefeaturelarry/casualties-together/ ), и впечатление у меня были примерно такие же, как у одиночной игры.

Your first few playthroughs *will* be a horrible experience. The game's audiovisual elements do a fantastic job conveying terror, agony, and ultimately death - arguably better than any other game I have played before. 

The challenges that the game throws at you feel insurmountable when you're still learning. I remember early on thinking to myself, "how on earth am I supposed to be able to stay alive long enough to craft anything remotely useful, let alone keep my Expie happy?". But over time you get better, and soon enough you will be able to have your Expie thrive in the first couple of layers. Once you get the hang of the game, scavenging and crafting and tending to your Expie's needs become a blast. You become adept at responding to emergencies when they arise. 

The fact that this is *just* the free demo is astounding to me. I absolutely cannot wait for the full release.

Если бы каждая демка имела такое же качество и проработку, мы бы сейчас жили в совсем другом мире....
Серьёзно, я впервые вижу выживач с такой проработанной системой здоровья, в которой аж используются настоящие медицинские термины. Обычно игры ограничиваются очками здоровья, выносливости, голода и жажды, а тут есть и сатурация (уровень кислорода в крови), и давление, и ритм сердцебиения, и частота дыхания, и иммунитет, и уровень инфекции и боли каждой конечности - всё это лечится отдельно и вручную разными медицинскими приспособлениями и реальными лекарствами, которые придётся изучать в гугле, если у вас нету медицинского образования (да, переломы и вывихи тоже здесь лечатся вручную). --- After First Time Playing: 2hrs ---

I think the game has a lot of potential. I will admit that this is going outside what I normally play, since I've always been scared to waste my time on games outside my comfort zone. But I still get around to playing games like this that gains my interest. My overall, short, review is: Play it with the expectation that you know nothing and will get nowhere in the first few tries of the game.

My more comprehensive, albeit relatively short, review will be in two parts:
1) Story
2) Gameplay

-Story-
The story premise hints at a company which taken over human civilization, which is rather vague to say the least. You are (and the specie name is) an "experiment", Expie for short. You're tasked as a disposable character for "the company" to retrieve a previous, unknown thing from an expedition gone wrong. You begin your journey in the decent pod and will end as a corpse in a cave, whether that be by "natural death" or s*icide.

I think the story is, or should be, second to the mechanics of the gameplay. I think it should stay that way because it helps set the scene but without detracting from what the game is mostly about, the gameplay. The word "company" can hint at anything, which helps avoid people bickering about *Insert econ/politic persuasion*. If the creator gets a bit more specific, then they should detail how "the company"  it operates. If the company did something bad, like enslave others and force others to fund their efforts, then that is what should be detailed. Rather than being explicit about preaching a certain message to a point it feels like a lecture. Irrespective of any persuasion, I've unfortunately seen bad storytelling like this and many times I fear that good games/media can be ruined by bad, lecture-like storytelling.

The story highlights the unforgiving, brutal side of human nature. Specifically when terrible humans have dehumanized their victims to further scientific discovery. The Expie is a specie, bioengineered by humans, that represents the literal dehumanization of what is a person as a matter of their idea of law. Instead, the Expie is treated as but an animal to be tested upon, do dangerous missions and disposed when not of use. This is the side of the story I think it should highlight. That bad people justify doing bad acts to a creation that should be considered a person, but their law doesn't recognize Expies as equal to humans.

-Gameplay-
The gameplay is brutal, even in the relaxed mode. Although it relatively is, I thought the relaxed mode would be a lot easier than the intended, default mode. I am a beginner to all of this, so of course there is a lot to learn on my end. The controls are less complicated than I thought. The real challenge is knowing how to navigate the basics then being thrown into a completely unknown environment and with zero knowledge on what to do next. You just explore, hope to survive and be cautious about making fatal mistake. When you die, you learn from your Expie's death and move on with the next Expie you control.

When I came across a survivor, it felt like a breath of fresh air and safety. The trading mechanics are interesting, but I didn't really get a chance to explore that in depth. What I do know is that you have a few options to get a good deal out of the trade. It ranges from neutral, bad and positive options that will affect the reputation you have with the trader. With this, I hope that the developer rewards peaceful trading. But they disincentivize hostility to temporarily reduce prices, it may work in the short run but will be more difficult in the long run. Thus, having to really weigh your options prior to making a decision. You may be despite, so you choose hostility. But when you're in better condition, you may come across a survivor that will have increased prices for you due to your previous hostility.

The only main criticism I have for the game is how it teaches the player to play the game. I think that it is REALLY brutal as someone who has done no prior research searching up "how to guides" on YouTube, or any other media sharing platform. It would be in theme if I could come across survivors that you can trade currency or other resource for their service to teach you how to do *insert mechanic here*. You could do tutorials like when I first booted up the game, but I think that doesn't fit so well with the theme that your Expie is but a disposable creature. Relying on survivors to gain this information would fit perfectly in my opinion.

The game is truly at its best after having made a grave error. The intensity of seeing if you have the resources at hand to salvage the run, and if not, how long you can keep your heart beating to try and scrape together the resources to recover, makes this a seriously harrowing experience, especially as you get attached to each of your expies.

I do hope the concept get expanded upon further. Right now there's only 7 medical minigames, and you'll most frequently find yourself bandaging wounds and pulling shrapnel out of yourself. Minigames like amputation seem to never come up in my runs, requiring that a wound get so deeply infected and I somehow have no means of disinfecting the wound but have a knife ready at hand and enough bandages to stem the blood loss. Given that one of the most common plants in the game has a fruit that can be used to prevent or recover from infections, this is largely impractical.

Regardless, for a demo there is a huge amount of content here, enough that it could easily justify being a full release all on its own. I think really my biggest gripe is just the fact you can't save just anywhere you want, only when between the layers of the planet. Each one usually takes me close to an hour to finish so there's pretty long gaps between save points. Still an amazing experience if you can stomach the heavy subject matter. Highly recommended.

the systems in this game are so reactive and it feels really rewarding to learn and master them. i love a game that lets you discover what is going on over the hood through interaction - often times you need to make a judgement on whether or not it is relevant to use a specific item in a situation. it genuinely ends up helping to tap into your knowledge of first aid/medicine to glean what can be done.

the UI can be clunky, admittedly. i think fiddling with things and learning where they are is part of the challenge. the game is clearly supposed to be stressful to play. you're supposed to lose. if you hate that in a game, you probably won't enjoy the experience that is being simulated here. this game is also especially not for you if you are particularly susceptible to depictions of self-harm, gore, suicide. oh, and spiders!

The closest example for me would be like a mix of Barotrauma's Darkness, Isolation, Medical system and horror but without your submarine / crew. It also reminds me of Starbound / Early game Terraria with the caves, where misjudging distance can quickly get you injured or killed. This game is astoundingly good, like wow. it takes the concept of you merely telling someone what to do instead of controlling them and executes it perfectly. there were many times where i did something i really shouldn't have and the game very much let me know. It does a great job of giving the player character a lot of personality with a few simple lines. For example, i was trying to drink some lemonade from a barrel, and the first drink resulted in my expie saying "i would rather starve". i didn't think anything of it and drank again, to which my expie said "is this some kind of punishment?" It made me feel SO BAD about it like no other game can. Instead of saying something like "oh ♥♥♥♥" when i fall and break my leg, i say "I'm so sorry" because the disconnect between player and character is just wide enough that you develop a connection with them. it also happens when your expie is refusing to do things they really should do, like grab a bandage to try to cover up major bleeding, where ill find myself getting extremely frustrated at the expie themselves, rather than the game. when your expie gets brain damage, they start slurring their speech and cant read fluidly anymore, again makes me feel SO BAD for putting them through that. It makes you really care about them, and every careless mistake really weighs on you. the death of each expie is often slow and agonizing for them, while you frantically try to save them, while also battling their confusion, brain damage, and unwillingness to do what you say anymore. you dont ever feel the need to restart, because it involves the expies brain chip ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ exploding, and they cry out in fear during it. Its all so perfect.

The health mechanics are a little on the annoying side with infections and the relative rarity of antiseptics, but its not meant to be forgiving, again feeding into making you feel bad for carelessly jumping into a pit you didn't know was 100m deep, or running into barbed wire and getting cuts all over.

i dont know what it is about them, but the expie is one of the only characters i would love to have be real and be able to meet and befriend. they are just so lovable and have so much hope in them (when they arent trying to kill themselves to escape the pain you caused), again, making it so much worse when they are brutalized.

i do have a few minor gripes though. one is that survivors are extremely rare to come across, ive only ever seen one in my 10 hours currently. this does make sense but maybe it could use a slight number change.
another is that the game feels too fast and too slow at the same time. there is an hour time limit for each layer and im always nearing it, yet so many things are happening that it all feels like a blur. again, makes sense from a narrative standpoint but it might need some tweaking, (not sure how that would work but idk, its my review) and also with that, the sleep mechanic is a bit odd, since energy levels always seem to go down extremely fast. another is that falling is VERY punishing, since you ragdoll and continue falling until you are caught by something. and if you get knocked out while falling, or carried by water from a geyser, then good luck. and another is that traps are a bit braindead, being just seemingly randomly scattered, put into wildly inconvenient places, and easily avoided if you are paying attention and exercising caution. and one thing i would like to see in the full release is a proper ending, where you actually find the cargo and are able to retrieve it and be spared. of course, there will always be more to get back.

those gripes are from a player enjoyment perspective though, and like i said, it makes sense from a narrative standpoint, where nothing will be comfortable, convenient, or in your favor at all. it is an amazing game and i will buy and play the full release 100%. also multiplayer would be unlike anything else, could be an amazing canvas for character interactions.


all that aside though, you have to be in the position to like this game, especially in its current state. a lot of people mention the rng factor, and yeah, its rough. while i personally dont mind it (again, narrative sense), crafting things like flashlights and other essential tools doesnt come up often, as they require a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of materials that takes a lot of patience to get, and luck in getting containers for all of it too. the game is also VERY sadistic, where every little thing is made to make you feel bad. ive already said why i like this, but i see why many dont, and brush it off as a game where all its substance is "look what you did, dont you feel bad?"

anyway, my personal rating is a 9/10, a very unexplored genre that is being served well by this game. the main thing holding it back for many it its angsty content, but its more this genre of game that's the culprit, since it needs to have a bit of sadism and/or guilt tripping for it to take effect, this game just does it really well imo.

This is a very impressive survival that has the cavediver-ness without it being some sort of horror joke, its the grueling reality where any slip and fall will end someones life. 

Every single inch of medical function is extensively covered in this game and as someone with the insistent need for details for stimuli/function(largely due to autism²) this scratches my brain well. I have always had a deep fascination with medical things along with the desire for games to be more "real" with detail without killing the fantasy- and this game HITS.
  The fantastic loop of tense situations,discovery,and survival is hooking. the environment may feel familiar to other games but has PLEANTY of texture and new nuance that shock you out of that comfort zone . It is a extremely fresh and well crafted experience +impeccable sound design.
I feel extremely immersed in the world and determined to keep my expie healthy and alive. i get locked into the proces of gathering,prepping,staying alert, its a good feeling when you're keeping on top of things and get stacked. 

  Everything is compact and simulated in a pretty neat way!
Speaking of the health system it heavily triggers my medical anxiety and i have been using it for slow exposure therapy to reduce the anxiety, and it slightly goes over my developed hyper-vigilance ocd 
  But Its extremely overwhelming at first for many,and thats completely fine for people who are used to more simple health systems to get bombarded by so much and get paralyzed in how to do it "right" when they are just curious about the environment . 

I see people procrastinate on the PANEL in the health menu and its funny haha- i briefly did too! 
[h1] heres some tips: [/h1]

1. 
[b]Most important[/b] is your blood , heartrate, and immunity. if either of those are irregular/bad something is very very wrong and you need to learn how to fix it.
 Out of everything though.. i keep my eyes LOCKED on the blood level

2.
Keep your food&water FULL whenever you can . your weight dropping makes everything much harder. the best way to think is that your sweet little expie HUNGERS and has a fast metabolism , but can be satiated for a decent amount of time. exercise will drop your weight and hunger , extra tip this also makes you tired quicker (it accelerates the base tiredness ticking down).
Meats and anything fatty is your friend(just dont get sick)

3.
Be heavily observant, the game rewards attention to detail and keeping your eyes peeled is the best way to start . do not be careless for a fraction of time. You have to sweep everything with your eyes as much as possible, practice it slowly on each run. moodles , environment, moodles , environment, moodles ,environment . repeat untill you can read information quicker and smarter. 

4.
Skin health is the most important thing next to the immunity mechanic.both will help you with infections. At a certain point if ur immunity is very low disinfectants will NOT work.


5.
Avoid water with broken bones.You WILL get stuck and drown if you have nothing for the pain. as soon as you are in deep water with a fracture, USE OPIUM OR PAIN KILLERS. so you can leave the water as fast as possible.also dont panic,it wastes energy spent digging out

(Most frustrating part of the adrenaline mechanic being so weak or basically non existent. which i mention later on)

6.
If not in immediate deep danger,its better to overestimate a dose and be skittish . if in critical condition its better to moderately dose and underestimate it , you NEED a kick when you will- skimping on a painkiller will cost you your life .still make sure not to OD. (CHECK IF ITS A DILUTED OR NOT DILUTED DOSE AND KEEP IT IN MIND!)

1. In my opinion
i think the crafting menu needs to be neater its too much to process , better organized with more immediate levels of craftables visible before you can open up other sections for the tougher ones. This demo is pretty freaking addicting.
If you enjoy Terraria's caving as much as I do, this is that but more kinetic and involved, and fleshed out into a full game.

The learning curve at the start is decently steep. The first layer can be brutal on initial runs, and the medical system will make you feel miserable as you struggle and are able to do nothing to stop the bleeding. 
And it will continue feeling like that until you learn how to spot traps and bad falls before you are killed by them. 

If you want my advice, focus on learning how to avoid traps as much as possible. 
Nothing else in this game, between the crafting, the medical system, and the starvation, matters as much to your early experiences as do the traps that will inflict the most instantaneous misery with the littlest opportunity to recover from.

In that regard, Relaxed mode is the best possible thing for new players to try, as it is a godsend for people who want to experience a difficult game, but can't deal with the misery of fighting the learning curve.
It is not an assist mode, it's the training grounds that gives you the same game with the same difficult experience, but with *more time*.

It changes very little about the gameplay. Traps do the same damage and appear in the same amounts. Instead, it gives you minor visibility improvements and lengthens the time you have, so that you're able to familiarize yourself with the game. It's not fun getting hit by traps you can't see. So, use relaxed mode to learn about what traps look like.

Oh, and get the multiplayer mod. 90% of my playtime is playing with friends, and it's such a ubiquitous facet of the games appeal to where even Orsoniks (the lead dev) has acknowledged that it adds a huge amount to the experience.

Besides sharing some beginner's advice, I do have some things to nitpick. But these are moreso things that I just want to see fixed with future updates.

The crafting mechanics are actually pretty good and detailed, but the menu design is awful. It feels like a first draft that hasn't been retouched since it was first developed. Opening it for the first time and being exposed to some 30-40 recipes at once sorted in a pretty much arbitrary manner left a really bad impression for me. The provided categorization tabs are hardly useful until you memorize which items are where. Searching for recipes is really cumbersome (having to enter the search bar to find items always grinds things to a halt and makes attempts at using a controller super unwieldy), and sorting items by the required INT level feels like it should be a toggle and not the only option. Dragging items to the bottom craft menu icon is a new addition and should 100% be added to the first tutorial. I didn't know it existed until after I'd finished with a whole crafting planner. 

Getting physically stuck inside of barbed wire always feels especially brutal.

There should be an accessibility feature for disabling or dimming the flashlight strobe effect.

Layer transitions feel clunky. The bottom of the layer feels awkward to stand on, the shake effects freezing on the loading screen feels unpolished, and getting dragged away by moving water or being sniped by a trap always feels bad, especially with custom setting runs.

Some tutorials being locked behind reaching layers 2 and 3 can be especially frustrating for players who think they need the tutorials. I might suggest moving the goal to being something closer, like 'reach 150m' and 'reach 450m` respectively, and/or perhaps not reveal that those tutorials exist until they're unlocked so that players don't feel like crucial information is being withheld.

When in the tutorial, the 'highlight' effect on UI items as they're being referenced is pretty low contrast with the health chip and can be hard to spot admist all of the pale green and the many numbers.

Where this game shines brightest is its incredibly authentic medical experience. Instead of generic hit‑points, it simulates full‑scale limb damage, blood loss, infection, pain shock and cardiovascular status. You have to disinfect wounds, splint fractures, watch out for drug side‑effects, and judge when to rest or keep pushing forward. A tiny mistake in treatment can snowball into a fatal disaster, and this makes taking care of your body feel genuinely high‑stakes.
The environment is relentlessly dangerous. Every layer of this alien planet hides hidden traps, environmental threats and unpredictable dangers. You are never truly safe; one misstep can ruin your whole run. The constant pressure creates amazing immersion, you will stay alert and nervous throughout your exploration.
It is brutal, challenging and deeply rewarding. For players craving realistic, unforgiving survival simulation, this game is an absolute gem. Definitely worth your time.

This game is extremely fun and I definitely recommend giving the demo a try to see how you like it. I do have my gripes with it, but its stuff that you can easily adjust in their custom difficulty mode, so it fine.

I love the advanced health system, and is obviously when you play it, one of the biggest parts of this game right now, any small mistake could lead to a ton of health problems. And they don't go easy on you. This game doesn't have multiplayer but there is a very nice mod on nexus that gives it, my partner, a friend, and I were playing together and that friend set off a sneaky landmine, which caused the death of all of us, but not instantly, we had the chance to survive if we had the right tools to use, and even if I for example did, my entire jaw was ripped off, so you could imagine the level of extra problems that could cause for me.

The stuff I don't like in this game, is a gripe I have for any game that does this and that is not difficult of the game itself, but the artificial ones. What I mean by this, is stuff that is just there to add difficulty, but it just doesn't make any sense to be there. Some examples, water flow moves your character, even the tiniest amount of flow can not only move you, but send your character into a ragdoll state and possibly fall a great height, there is no way to counter this without turning it off in the settings. Me and all my 110 lbs irl self could stand/walk in a flowing river knee deep and be just fine, but this little goober slips and falls when its barely even above his ankles.

The other example is with the menu system. I ran into a problem where I found a bottle of bleach, I went to put it in my inventory, realized it was full so I let go of it, and then 'oops I drank it.' Now you could see this as a 'skill issue' which it is a little bit, but the problem is the way the inventory works in general. When you press 'tab' it opens up a circle, the circle is your inventory, on the perimeter you have slots to put items in, those being in your mouth 'not consuming stuff just holding something there' your hands, upper, middle, and lower back. In the center of it is where you drag items you can 'use'. When I let go of right click for the bleach I was dragging into my inventory, it was over the 'use' option, no confirmation I wanted to do that, just consumed 25% instantly, which very much as you could imagine lead to my death, wasn't the main cause mind you, but it caused so many problems in my characters body that it basically was the reason. Why would I ever want to actually drink bleach? The death from it is not even fast and if I wanted to just end the round quickly, you can do that just by quitting the game (game doesn't save progress unless you use console command 'saveandquit'). Just add a confirmation on using items like that and it would be much better, or add a button to the use item section of the inventory. Instead of 'let go of right click on the slot to use' do 'hover over the slot and 'PRESS' left click to use' that simple change would fix all of that issue instantly.

All in all this game is amazing and most artificial difficulties besides the bleach one can easily be fixed by changing the game settings in custom difficulties.

TLDR: Great game, and pretty complete as a demo. Prepare to suffer and die a miserable death, time and time again. And as a wise OG said: I [b]l hate gravity![/b]

Now for a more serious review: this demo, as is, is very complete and can sustain you for quite a few hours, I reckon the first half of the game is there. The gameplay is great, it is very hard mostly because you need to know what to do and gather to make it through... and as you can imagine, when you start you don't know much.

You can either seek knowledge (wiki, experienced players, etc.) to have a grasp of what to do to increase your odds at survival, or you can ball. Death will come in many ways, most of them involving gravity and/or a myriad of hazards.

You have to manage your health (which is a pretty detailed system, but just make sure you're not bleeding like a fountain), thirst/hunger, body temperature (this will be quite an adventure starting from the desert layer), and your mood.

Speaking of which, there is a content warning at the start of the game because of the themes of misery, self-harm and all. If you mess up enough to get very depressed, you will cut yourself, or even gouge your eye out if you really mess up. 

Which leads us into the next part: the game manages to sell you the idea that you are not the character you play. You're just overseeing a critter sent among thousands to die on a suicide mission. What this can achieve (depends on you really) is you will feel responsible for your expie's safety and all ailments that come to them more than if it was just... you. The first few runs will likely not feel good once you reach an untimely end. But in the end, this game is all about hope and defiance before death.

Bonus note: there is a mod for multiplayer support around there. While I think the game is best experienced solo, playing with friends can bring you some extra comfort, fun, or memes. I will probably not forget the one time I had a bad fall, and my expie dropped the plasma cutter I was holding... which then flew right onto a landmine next to my friend who got the premium Bosnia special (he did not survive)

I first heard of this game during V3, and even though I knew the game was not complete yet I was hoping that there was some kind of objective or win condition. This game is special to me because the value of the life of the player character is extremely high not just because it features permadeath but also how expressive the creature is. That is why if you play this game now, you will essentially rob yourself out of playing a better game whenever this ends up being finished. The whole appeal of this game comes from figuring the game out and the artistic value behind the damage system, but both those systems lose their merit fast. I really wanted to like this game, but right now it feels more annoying than ever.

The atmosphere, concept, and survival mechanics are genuinely interesting, and there are moments in the game where overcoming difficulties actually feels satisfying. But unfortunately, all of these are overshadowed by unfair and nonsensical mechanics.

Many injuries feel unavoidable because the game expects you to not know things you never could predict on your first encounter. Instead of encouraging players to use environment for gaining experience, the game punishes players without any reason. This game is surprisingly easy, and because of that, almost all of your mistakes are intentionally caused by the game, which turns it from the hardcore survival simulator to the Microsoft Windows Minesweeper.

Trap design is the weakest point in this game. As I've understood it correctly, almost all of the traps can be completely bypassed by just simply digging underneath them, while others are perfectly placed in the darkest corner of the cave outside your screen, where the game teaches you that the slightest brush against a cactus causes a ragdoll by launching you straight into the nearest mine and ending your run. Another trap placement's major issue is that it's possible to find traps spawning inside life pods. Difficulty should come from meaningful choices and awareness, not from random ass spikes that leave no opportunity to react. 

Enemy variety is also lacking. After a while, encounters become repetitive, and the world starts to feel less dangerous than it should.

I love hardcore games, games that challenge the player's skill and attentiveness, not when they rely only on unavoidable deaths. I hope the release changes will focus on making the game's difficulty in a fair way, instead of making it unbearable.

I stumbled upon this game completely by chance, and I love it. I love how it captures people’s attention and lets them write their own tragedy. Everything about this game is amazing.
The music is absolutely incredible. I hope they release the soundtracks on Steam to give the creator more support (maybe even on Bandcamp). The story really catches my interest, and I’m excited to explore the entire backstory. The game is similar to Terraria, but with added platformer-style movements (like wall-jumping), and it’s much darker. The health mechanics are something that really interests me.

Now for the critical part of the game, I really miss the ability to save the game. The only way to save is to reach the end of a layer. If you rush through it, you’ll get there in about 10 minutes. And that’s about it. During my 7 hours of play, I didn’t find anything I didn’t like. It’s a brutal and challenging game. You never know where you’ll fall or what will fall on you.
Although I like the idea of multiplayer in this game, I don’t think it’s designed for multiplayer. You have to be there alone and really get into your character. When something explodes and injures your whole body, when you step on a piece of glass you thought you’d cleared away. Or when you’re just looking down.

I’m looking forward to buying this game as soon as it’s released.

Tense, intense, and addicting.
This game has *very* good bones. I have high hopes for where this game goes next, as it becomes fleshed out further(especially in it's medical mechanics). There is already a robust multiplayer mod available, to boot!

 The health simulation in this game is detailed, robust, and the first  I've seen of its kind I've seen in video game. Blood, for example: Get bitten by something venomous, your wound won't stop bleeding without bandaging, and it becomes dangerous to use wound glue to stop the bleeding. When dehydration kills, it does so by making the blood unbearably thick, causing pulmonary embolisms, causing suffocation. Blood pressure is modeled too, systolic and diastolic pressure. A systolic pressure too high will cause a hemorrhagic stroke (in one of my runs, happened after a combination of being over-hydrated, and exertion when trying to escape a pit of lumalge)(Beware of sudden partial blindness, and uninjured hands inexplicably becoming disabled).
The inter-connected health system includes/affects (but isn't limited to) mood, hunger, and immunity(all these mentioned here either affect are are affected by blood volume). Beware, there is nothing so simple as a hitpoint or debuff. The health panel does a good job of reminding you of this (though there is a mode without it, you will have to diagnose issues from vague cues; visual inspection and limited moodles).

The game, as many others can attest to, is brutally difficult, and you will often learn quickly (if you pay attention, something I was not good at, but I figured it out after many ended runs) through trial and error (and, it be quite a sad process for some, more on that later.). So I advise you: slow down! observe and see how you can take proper advantage of your environment! Do not ignore plants, they are your key to crafting what you need and staying well-fed. A big fall could be waiting below any missed jump that you were *sure* you could make.

I applaud Orsoniks for understanding how to embody that fear of severe injury and mortal danger, and convey pain. So much done with something so "simple." (which, considering the sort of games this developer has made previously, and how those games handled bloody violence.). This game does not need relentless, hulking alien monsters to make you scared (though there is one), and it does not need horrific, alien parasites/parasitoids in order to give you a sickening sense of uneasiness while observing encroaching sickness and degredation (those do not exist in the game, yet). For these reasons, the game can be emotionally gripping. There is something about this game that makes it difficult for players to project themselves on the character they control; instead they become attached (a strength, which, I think the game should play into more, if possible), as if it's life is in their hands. For that reason, it can be a cruel game. The game has much to show you for when you fail (and you will falter). The character will yelp and whine in pain, cry out to be saved when dying (remember how I said the trial and error can be a "quite a sad process"?) . You would see this as starvation leaves them weak and unable to fight off sepsis. When you don't take care of them, you watch what happens to them despair sets, eventually they would deciding to claw themselves to death, perhaps gouge out their eyes. Death is slow and grueling in this game. Not even stepping on a land mine will end things so quickly. The developer took special care to make the deaths haunting, with that grainy vignette of the dead body, laying on the cavern floor. Unlike the deaths, the things that bring it come suddenly. At the very least, though, the slowness of it means that if you are very well supplied (and not being swarmed/eaten alive), you can survive almost any trap or fall.

Even the first layer, for lack of knowledge, causes many deaths, for that reason, I heavily recommend the tutorials (the last two that exist thus are earned by crossing into the second and third layers respectively). I am bad at closings, so I will end this with some general tips:

Starting a run, collect two plastic chunks to make a canteen, make as much bio-chemical fluid as possible (it's useful for many recipes. You can't separate fluids(without a centrifuge), but you may choose to store other crafting fluids you don't consider otherwise useful in the same container, you may eventually want to switch to an I.V. bag (it is craftable) for this, eventually, as it is larger capacity and more weight efficient. Press F to favorite items to forbid their use in crafting). Craft any cheap and easy items you can; crafting each item for the first time gives you experience in the Int attribute, leveling up lets you craft more advanced items and lets you identify more items, like valuable medicines that can pull a run back from the brink. Life-pod chests contain blueprints which help you level up.

Enemies can be stunned and damaged by throwing objects. Sadly, ceiling rye can't be harvested by throwing things. 

Jump pads can become very dangerous in proximity to traps and worsen potential falls. They can become dangerous by being in tight corridors, and induce a brutal cycle of being thrown up into the ceiling, this can cause debilitating brain damage and internal bleeding. I am sure this aspect of the jump pad has caused it's share of casualties for the player base. These traps can be made temporarily safe. Figure out how, yourself, and bask in your own intellect.

Turn on darker backgrounds in the settings — this can help you differentiate background from foreground, so you can judge tricky jumps. It really seemed to help me navigate the terrain, judging vaguely from memory, hard to say. It seems to have saved me from an unknown number of preventable falls.

Do not ignore the plants (ignoring plants is perhaps the worst mistake newer players make; I know this from both experience and observation)! Break the geotrees and eat the fruit, stay well-fed and hydrated. The plants have important crafting material to offer. Hold shift to while hovering any item you aren't familiar with, for more information.

You can just bandage over shrapnel and remove the shrapnel later. The game doesn't too that good of a job communicating this, but bandages slow bleeding over time, meaning you don't have to use as much as you think, when the blood drop icon changes to being wrapped in gauze(meaning a long bandage effect duration), when you see that, you can prioritize more urgent injuries. Don't be too stingy with bandages! Low skin health increases infection chance on a limb (Improperly tended wounds have cost me some runs, one way or another.).

невероятная проработка здоровья персонажа. условное кровотечение это не просто эффект банальной потери единичек хп (привет тарков). кровь в этой игре это отдельная наука со своими приколами, у крови есть своя вязкость, насыщенность кислородом. слишком большая потеря крови и концентрации кислорода в ней приводит к быстрой потере температуры тела. когда кровопотери слишком сильные, может начаться фибрилляция, остановить которую можно дефибриллятором, звучит просто, но нужно поймать идеальный размер заряда относительно молниеносно сокращающегося ритма сердцебиения пока на экране и в ушах происходит безумие.
также у персонажа имеется ментальное здоровье в зависимости от состояния которого он может по разному реагировать на вещи. при плохом настроении он может иногда отказываться что либо делать. если дело доходит до депрессии - он начнёт превращать свои руки в вишнёвые слойки. а если персонаж наоборот счастлив - в случае резких смертельных ранений он может буквально вернуться с того света (не без побочек)

это нетипичный рогалик, он заставит вас ОЧЕНЬ сильно стрессовать даже не показывая противников на экране. (стресс получаемый от игры кратно множится когда у прокладки между монитором и стулом есть эмпатия к несуществующим персонажам в компьютерных игрушках.) 

я безумно жду релиза и готов заплатить. контента в демке уже хватает как на полноценную игру (молчу про моды на полноценный ко-оп и просто моды на новый контент и углубление базовых механик).
это НЕ фурри игра, фурри начинаются и заканчиваются на дизайне персонажа, отставьте предвзятость.
